name: Contrarian take
whenToUse: You disagree with common advice developers keep hearing. Strongest share driver for expert accounts.
hookPatterns: Stop [common advice]. It's [why it's wrong].
Unpopular opinion: [belief most devs hold] is wrong.
Everyone says [X]. After [credential], I think it's backwards.
beats: Hook: name the common belief and reject it in one line
Credential in one clause (why you get to say this)
The real reason it's wrong, with one concrete example
Punchline or CTA that invites disagreement in comments
visualPlan: Avatar wide on hook, tight on the credential, card for the 'instead' rule, avatar wide for CTA.
exampleHooks: Stop doing LeetCode to get your first dev job.
Unpopular opinion: you don't need a vector database for RAG.

name: I built X with AI
whenToUse: You have a screen recording of something real you built. Highest credibility format for a technical audience.
hookPatterns: I built [useful thing] in [short time] with [tool]. Here's how.
This [thing] used to take me [long time]. Now it takes [short time].
beats: Hook: show the finished result first, state the time/effort
CTA: comment a keyword for the repo/template
visualPlan: Avatar hook (≤3s), then split layout: screen recording top, avatar bottom. End on avatar wide.
exampleHooks: I built a RAG chatbot over my own YouTube transcripts in 20 minutes.

name: Myth vs reality
whenToUse: A widely-repeated claim about tech careers or AI that you can correct with experience.
hookPatterns: '[Myth].' That's a myth. Here's what actually happens.
You've been told [myth]. I've seen [N] cases. It's not true.
beats: Hook: state the myth on a card
Proof: a stat, a story fragment, or an example
So what: what the viewer should do
visualPlan: Card with the myth (strike-through feel), avatar for reality, b-roll during proof.
exampleHooks: 'AI will replace junior developers.' Here's what I'm actually seeing in hiring.

name: N things
whenToUse: Packable, saveable advice. Keep N at 3 so each item gets a real beat.
hookPatterns: 3 [skills/tools/mistakes] that [outcome].
If I were [situation] in 2026, I'd learn these 3 things.
beats: Hook with the number and the payoff
Item 3 (the best one, saved for last)
visualPlan: Card per item number, avatar delivering each item, alternate wide/tight framing every beat.
exampleHooks: 3 AI skills that will get you hired faster than another React project.

name: AI news, what it means for devs
whenToUse: Something shipped in the last 48 hours. Speed beats polish; this is the best use of the clone.
hookPatterns: [Company] just shipped [thing]. Here's what it means if you're a developer.
Everyone's hyping [release]. Here's the part nobody's talking about.
beats: Hook: the news in one line
Why it matters for working developers / job seekers
visualPlan: Split layout with a screenshot/screen recording of the announcement on top, avatar below. Avatar wide for the take.
exampleHooks: OpenAI just changed how agents work. Here's what that means for your job search.

name: X explained in 30 seconds
whenToUse: A concept your audience hears constantly but can't define (RAG, embeddings, agents, MCP).
hookPatterns: [Concept] explained like you're a developer, not a data scientist.
You keep hearing about [concept]. Here it is in 30 seconds.
visualPlan: Cards for each step, avatar between cards. B-roll only if concrete.
exampleHooks: RAG explained in 30 seconds, for developers.

name: Hiring manager POV
whenToUse: Lean on your experience hiring and mentoring developers. Authority hook.
hookPatterns: I've [hired/mentored] [N] developers. This is what gets people rejected.
As someone who reviews resumes: [specific red flag].
beats: Why it matters to the person hiring
visualPlan: Avatar tight on the credential, b-roll of resumes/interviews, card for the fix.
exampleHooks: I've mentored hundreds of career changers. This one resume line kills your chances.

name: My mistake
whenToUse: A real failure with a cost attached. Film this one yourself: viewers punish an AI face on personal stories.
hookPatterns: I wasted [time/money] on [thing]. Don't do what I did.
Biggest mistake I made [doing X].
visualPlan: Real footage. If using the pipeline, use it only for captions and cutaways over your own clip.
exampleHooks: I spent $40k building a feature nobody used.

name: Reply to a comment
whenToUse: A real comment or DM question. Native-feeling and drives more comments.
hookPatterns: Someone asked: '[question]'. Here's my honest answer.
'[Pushback comment].' Let me explain.
beats: Hook: read the question (card shows it)
visualPlan: Card styled as the comment for the hook, avatar for the answer.
exampleHooks: 'Is it too late to learn to code in 2026?' Honest answer.

name: If I were starting today
whenToUse: Career-changer audience. A concrete path beats general encouragement.
hookPatterns: If I had to become a [role] in [timeframe] starting today, here's exactly what I'd do.
The [N]-step roadmap I give every career changer.
visualPlan: Cards for each step with a running checklist feel, avatar between, b-roll of focused work.
exampleHooks: If I had to become an AI engineer in 6 months starting today, here's exactly what I'd do.

name: The software bill math
whenToUse: Business owners paying monthly for software they half-use. Make the cost concrete, then show owning it is now realistic.
hookPatterns: You're paying [$/mo] for [software] and using 10% of it.
Add up what you pay for software every year. Now look at what a custom build costs in 2026.
beats: Hook: the recurring bill, made concrete (example math at list price)
What you actually use vs what you pay for
Why owning it used to be unrealistic (six figures, months)
What changed: AI lets one senior engineer rebuild just the parts you use, for a fixed price
How it works / who it's for
visualPlan: Avatar hook, cards for the numbers (big, simple), avatar for what changed, card for who it's not for, avatar CTA.
exampleHooks: A 10-person team on four apps pays about fifteen grand a year. Every year.
Add up what you pay every month for software. Now multiply by forever.

name: Your software is a landlord
whenToUse: Reframe SaaS as rent. Emotional, shareable, owner-to-owner tone.
hookPatterns: Your CRM is a landlord. It collects rent every month and raises it every year.
Fire your software. It's been on the payroll long enough.
beats: The cost of renting forever (price hikes, per seat)
The alternative: own one app built around how you work
What owning means (fixed price, your code, no seats)
visualPlan: Avatar hook wide, card for the rent math, avatar tight for 'own it', card for the 3 terms, avatar CTA.
exampleHooks: Fire your software. It's been on the payroll long enough.

name: See it before you pay
whenToUse: Handle the risk objection: custom software means paying before you see anything. The 24-hour demo flips that.
hookPatterns: Most software quotes ask you to pay before you see anything. I flip that.
What if you could see your own version of your software before paying a cent?
beats: Hook: the usual risk (pay first, wait months)
The flip: see a working demo of your version first
How it works in 3 steps (form, 10-minute call, demo in 24 hours if it's a fit)
Like it, I build it. Don't, you owe nothing
visualPlan: Avatar hook, cards for the 3 steps, split screen with demo footage if available, avatar CTA.
exampleHooks: Most software quotes ask you to pay before you see anything.

name: The per-seat trap
whenToUse: Growing businesses where every hire raises the software bill.
hookPatterns: Every new hire comes with a new software bill.
Grow your team, not your software bill.
beats: Show the math growing with headcount (example)
The alternative: one app you own, hire as many people as you want
How to find out what yours would cost
visualPlan: Avatar hook, card showing seats x price growing, avatar for the alternative, avatar CTA.
exampleHooks: Every new hire comes with a new software bill.
